title: Anxiety
excerpt: Reasoning (and crying) my way through fascist AI-induced anxiety.
content_html:
Anxiety is usually different to stress only insofar as it is persistent and remains even after the stressor departs. But AI is apparently ever present, always intertwined with everything... so who knows what I feel. I struggle to really comprehend how unwell I am sometimes because of the erosion of what feels like everything, turbocharged by AI. Since joining an AI-related department 5 years ago, for me at least, everything has become fully infected.

I'm going to lay out some thoughts with the hope maybe this exercise provides something helpful to others, serves as healing for myself, and possibly and eventually places a small pebble on the road to getting us all out of this mess — like Nikhil Suresh says "to reassure the people trying to survive amidst all of this that they are not crazy." Also thanks to those like Lauren Fraser who said that they may be interested in hearing what I am about to regurgitate below.

You may wonder what this emotional extraction and turmoil has to do with AI. It has everything to do with AI. Or rather AI has everything to do with it. Emotional extraction and oppression is enacted by AI — and these forces run on similar lines whereby psychological exhaustion of the more vunlerable plays an active role in keeping us in place.

From another angle: simply put, fascist AI and all its symptoms force some of us academics to confront our complicity, our intertwinededness, and the moral imperative to take a stand. I will not be silently complicit in extracting from mentees and students, whether its their data, their emotional and cognitive labour, or anything else. I will not stand by and allow the university to be hollowed out and destroyed. An imperfect institution needs to be improved, not sold to the lowest bidder — or sadly and more accurately, should not pay a subscription to the evillest corporation.

Abdaljawad Omar outlines Western academia and society in general as

"a listening subject already fortified against the implications of what it hears, a political discourse that turns truth into noise, that converts even the most exhaustive documentation into the occasion for another round of managed uncertainty, and that has learned to wear the grammar of intelligence as its instrument of foreclosure. [...] The Western intellectual's cowardice is real: the fork in the road existed, the choice was made, the responsibility is not dissolved by calling it structural."

In the time of AI enabled genocide in Palestine, where we watch AI companies clamour to facilitate the USA's attack on Iran, as well as openly flaunting their contributions to planetary destruction, we are also witnessing the loss of the university. We sell out to companies so much, it's not even on all people's radars as a conflict of interest. We had one job. Our role as academics is to protect this one institution. This is why we receive tax money; why we're basically civil servants. The role of the university is even lost on many, so bears repeating: produce knowledge and educate at the highest level. AI destroys both at their core. It exposes some of us as confused, some of us as opportunistic, and both groups as cowards who would rather extract than reflect, would rather move fast and break things than learn to follow the slow and methodical praxis of scholarly work.

AI enters the fray

This emotional extraction and turmoil is also very personal. Who as an academic in their right mind would not feel betrayed, angry, unhinged — a shattering of our worldview — at the discovery that our colleagues, our superiors, those who manage the university at every level are fine with all this? They are fine with complicity in genocide, in scholasticide at home as well as abroad, in the destruction of their own university itself.

I have cried and lost sleep countless times... a new day a new chance for a loss of faith, for new levels of anything from anxiety to fear to depression to a braid of all the above. Why do so many of my colleagues, especially those with power to act, not see it? Why do they not care? We all who ask, in pain not in true questioning, know why. AI is a fascist project that enables and is enabled by all these interlocking events. And we've even been here before.

This emotional extraction and turmoil also extends to everything. The realisation the students are being pushed into this morass too: Can I trust my own mentees? I have caught myself thinking that a student's work is AI-generated when I had no good reason to. Just because the work was exceptionally good, something we had worked on together over months, I, anxiety-ridden and my trust in everybody fragile, reasoned it could be infected by AI. I went into the files and I looked at the historical edits. There was no evidence of AI, but just the dawning realisation that I and others like me could lose our grip, have lost our grip, on what trusting a colleague or a mentee means. I should have had the confidence to trust my junior collaborator without looking at the edit history.

I hated myself deeply in that moment. I remember crying so much. I also had flashbacks to many other unpleasant feelings of rejection from colleagues over my principles, over research areas, over the mere idea that certain people actually do deserve their voices heard, finally. It all mixes together in such moments. I really let it all get to me.

The second time these thoughts came over me, familiar but the memory did not help stop the anxiety from regrowing, festering. I felt so unwell and hated myself so much for thinking these thoughts, for accusing somebody even if just in my mind. I went to bed for about two days. Why should I be perpendicular to the world when I want it to go away?

As academics, we keep asking our employer to listen to us, to understand that our demands are about the future of the university as an institution, about the toppling of expertise and skill-learning as we know it. We don't want Microsoft's nonsense products. But we also do not want the frames and rhetoric from industry; we refuse the maliciously designed concepts, the pathetically framed sales pitches, the arguments from ignorance. No, if AI is a vague term, one cannot conclude some AI may be useful. No, Google's Alphafold is not scientific and not a different kind of technology. It's built on very similar formalisms — and perhaps even more importantly, constitutes the corporate capture of biology. Yes, such models are barely scientific. Thank goodness Google has killed it both as a product and as an excuse for these kinds of anti-scientific claims.

AI's way of thinking is not just anti-science, but spills into pseudoscience and other forms of complete detachment from reality. Core to the anxiety I am experiencing is that I feel so many around me have become unmoored from ethical and practical concerns, like keeping universities going, and attached instead to nonsense, to put it mildly. Nikhil Suresh explains this:

"Executives that tell the press that their company has gone insane will quickly find themselves removed from their positions. Employees who are honest will find themselves fired in short-order, or 'randomly' selected for a round of layoffs. In fact, it is in the interests of almost every actor in the space — boards, executives, employees, vendors, consultants — to obfuscate and misrepresent the success rate of AI projects. Many publicly traded companies are putting out announcements about their AI productivity gains when I know for a fact that the businesses have done nothing other than purchase Copilot licenses and declare victory."

Universities have done this too. And we best listen to those who blow these whistles before it's too late.

OK, so I had a few panic attacks because I realised the fabric of trust between me and my students, especially my closer mentees, was pretty thin. And also damaged is the belief that my colleagues, and even the university in general, have similar goals, like a love of learning and of teaching, a respect and appreciation for our jobs, a deep care for the psychological landscapes we all inhabit, and a need to cultivate our social relationships. Recall how like AI extracts labour, I witness senior colleagues extract from juniors their mental, and especially emotional, labour, offloading stress and cognitive processing onto others. And most disturbingly, pushing onto them this labour in their time of need. AI's logics do this to us too. Attacking educators and researchers is not a coincidence, but a group of people vulnerable after many rounds of funding cuts and anti-scientific and anti-humanistic thinking.

So what can we learn from this? Well, firstly, the obvious: be kind to ourselves if we feel the walls closing in because... well, yes, they are, so we need all the mental and physical fortitude we can muster. But, and perhaps more importantly than the well-known "take care of ourselves and others", we must keep at the forefront: this is what AI companies want. They want us to falter and get sick. They want us to have panic attacks, which sure, we will have, but — and this is the really vital bit — we will strive not to resolve the panic by allowing AI logics in.

Argument from ignorance, which a panic attack might trigger, is not valid: there is no good AI, just because it's a confusing terminological mess. The same goes for descent into using AI-detection tools. Just because some prose may look like it's written using an AI tool, in fact there is no such thing as automated plagiarism detection software. They are a scam sold by the very same companies that create the AI systems used for plagiarism in the first place. And companies through such so-called tools want to further erode our trust in each other.

Nor is it OK to allow AI to rule us by guiding our teaching — in fact I and my coauthors implore us not to

"allow AI, neither as bully nor so-called tool, to redefine our roles as educators or researchers. It is not our job to chase hype. What this means is by all means educators should feel empowered and inspired by the urgency to uplift students, but not to use AI to do so."

We also do not need to obey in advance as some love to do under increasing fascism. As Timothy Snyder explains:

"Most of the power of authoritarianism is freely given. In times like these, individuals think ahead about what a more repressive government will want, and then offer themselves without being asked. A citizen who adapts in this way is teaching power what it can do."

In our capacity as academics, perhaps the most radical thing we can do is our job itself. How can anybody in their right mind notice the growing damage to universities and instead of stand against this, facilitate the destruction of expertise, of learning skills, and of academic integrity? And the simplest stand is to refuse all the frames that want us scared and distrustful and instead embrace just doing our jobs and supporting each other.

They are fine with complicity in genocide, in scholasticide at home as well as abroad, in the destruction of their own university itself.

sentences.en: This emotional extraction and turmoil is also very personal.
sentences.zh: 这种情感的抽离和骚动也是非常个人化的。

sentences.en: Who as an academic in their right mind would not feel betrayed, angry, unhinged — a shattering of our worldview — at the discovery that our colleagues, our superiors, those who manage the university at every level are fine with all this?
sentences.zh: 作为一名心智正常的学者，当我们发现我们的同事、上级以及大学各个层面的管理人员都对这一切感到满意时，谁不会感到被背叛、愤怒、精神错乱——这是我们世界观的粉碎？

sentences.en: They are fine with complicity in genocide, in scholasticide at home as well as abroad, in the destruction of their own university itself.
sentences.zh: 他们对共谋种族灭绝、国内外的校园屠杀、破坏自己的大学本身并不介意。

blocks.html_en: I have cried and lost sleep countless times... a new day a new chance for a loss of faith, for new levels of anything from anxiety to fear to depression to a braid of all the above. Why do so many of my colleagues, especially those with power to act, not see it? Why do they not care? We all who ask, in pain not in true questioning, know why. AI is a fascist project that enables and is enabled by all these interlocking events. And we've even been here before.

sentences.en: I have cried and lost sleep countless times...
sentences.zh: 我无数次哭泣、失眠……

sentences.en: a new day a new chance for a loss of faith, for new levels of anything from anxiety to fear to depression to a braid of all the above.
sentences.zh: 新的一天是失去信心的新机会，是从焦虑到恐惧到抑郁再到上述所有情况的新水平。

sentences.en: Why do so many of my colleagues, especially those with power to act, not see it?
sentences.zh: 为什么我的很多同事，尤其是那些有权力采取行动的同事却看不到这一点？

sentences.en: Why do they not care?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么不关心？

sentences.en: We all who ask, in pain not in true questioning, know why.
sentences.zh: 我们所有带着痛苦而不是真正提问的人都知道为什么。

sentences.en: AI is a fascist project that enables and is enabled by all these interlocking events.
sentences.zh: 人工智能是一个法西斯项目，它促成了所有这些环环相扣的事件。

sentences.en: And we've even been here before.
sentences.zh: 我们以前来过这里。

blocks.html_en: This emotional extraction and turmoil also extends to everything. The realisation the students are being pushed into this morass too: Can I trust my own mentees? I have caught myself thinking that a student's work is AI-generated when I had no good reason to. Just because the work was exceptionally good, something we had worked on together over months, I, anxiety-ridden and my trust in everybody fragile, reasoned it could be infected by AI. I went into the files and I looked at the historical edits. There was no evidence of AI, but just the dawning realisation that I and others like me could lose our grip, have lost our grip, on what trusting a colleague or a mentee means. I should have had the confidence to trust my junior collaborator without looking at the edit history.

sentences.en: This emotional extraction and turmoil also extends to everything.
sentences.zh: 这种情感的抽离和骚动也延伸到了一切事物上。

sentences.en: The realisation the students are being pushed into this morass too: Can I trust my own mentees?
sentences.zh: 意识到学生们也被推入这个泥潭：我可以相信我自己的学员吗？

sentences.en: I have caught myself thinking that a student's work is AI-generated when I had no good reason to.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己在没有充分理由的情况下认为学生的作业是人工智能生成的。

sentences.en: Just because the work was exceptionally good, something we had worked on together over months, I, anxiety-ridden and my trust in everybody fragile, reasoned it could be infected by AI.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为这项工作非常好，我们一起工作了几个月，我就焦虑不安，而且我对每个人的信任都很脆弱，我认为它可能会被人工智能感染。

sentences.en: I went into the files and I looked at the historical edits.
sentences.zh: 我查看了文件并查看了历史编辑。

sentences.en: There was no evidence of AI, but just the dawning realisation that I and others like me could lose our grip, have lost our grip, on what trusting a colleague or a mentee means.
sentences.zh: 没有人工智能的证据，但只是逐渐意识到我和其他像我一样的人可能会失去我们的控制，已经失去了对信任同事或受训者意味着什么的控制。

sentences.en: I should have had the confidence to trust my junior collaborator without looking at the edit history.
sentences.zh: 我应该有信心相信我的初级合作者，而无需查看编辑历史记录。

blocks.html_en: I hated myself deeply in that moment. I remember crying so much. I also had flashbacks to many other unpleasant feelings of rejection from colleagues over my principles, over research areas, over the mere idea that certain people actually do deserve their voices heard, finally. It all mixes together in such moments. I really let it all get to me.

sentences.en: I hated myself deeply in that moment.
sentences.zh: 那一刻我深深地恨自己。

sentences.en: I remember crying so much.
sentences.zh: 我记得哭得很厉害。

sentences.en: I also had flashbacks to many other unpleasant feelings of rejection from colleagues over my principles, over research areas, over the mere idea that certain people actually do deserve their voices heard, finally.
sentences.zh: 我还闪回了许多其他不愉快的感觉，因为同事们拒绝了我的原则、研究领域，以及某些人实际上确实值得听到他们的声音的想法。

sentences.en: It all mixes together in such moments.
sentences.zh: 在这样的时刻，一切都混合在一起。

sentences.en: I really let it all get to me.
sentences.zh: 我真的让这一切都发生在我身上。

blocks.html_en: The second time these thoughts came over me, familiar but the memory did not help stop the anxiety from regrowing, festering. I felt so unwell and hated myself so much for thinking these thoughts, for accusing somebody even if just in my mind. I went to bed for about two days. Why should I be perpendicular to the world when I want it to go away?

sentences.en: The second time these thoughts came over me, familiar but the memory did not help stop the anxiety from regrowing, festering.
sentences.zh: 第二次这些想法出现在我脑海中时，我感到很熟悉，但记忆无助于阻止焦虑重新滋长、溃烂。

sentences.en: I felt so unwell and hated myself so much for thinking these thoughts, for accusing somebody even if just in my mind.
sentences.zh: 我感到非常不舒服，非常讨厌自己有这些想法，指责别人，即使只是在我的脑海里。

sentences.en: I went to bed for about two days.
sentences.zh: 我睡了大约两天。

sentences.en: Why should I be perpendicular to the world when I want it to go away?
sentences.zh: 当我希望世界消失时，为什么我应该垂直于世界？

blocks.html_en: As academics, we keep asking our employer to listen to us, to understand that our demands are about the future of the university as an institution, about the toppling of expertise and skill-learning as we know it. We don't want Microsoft's nonsense products. But we also do not want the frames and rhetoric from industry; we refuse the maliciously designed concepts, the pathetically framed sales pitches, the arguments from ignorance. No, if AI is a vague term, one cannot conclude some AI may be useful. No, Google's Alphafold is not scientific and not a different kind of technology. It's built on very similar formalisms — and perhaps even more importantly, constitutes the corporate capture of biology. Yes, such models are barely scientific. Thank goodness Google has killed it both as a product and as an excuse for these kinds of anti-scientific claims.

sentences.en: As academics, we keep asking our employer to listen to us, to understand that our demands are about the future of the university as an institution, about the toppling of expertise and skill-learning as we know it.
sentences.zh: 作为学者，我们不断要求雇主倾听我们的意见，了解我们的要求是关于大学作为一个机构的未来，关于推翻我们所知道的专业知识和技能学习。

sentences.en: We don't want Microsoft's nonsense products.
sentences.zh: 我们不想要微软的无意义产品。

sentences.en: But we also do not want the frames and rhetoric from industry; we refuse the maliciously designed concepts, the pathetically framed sales pitches, the arguments from ignorance.
sentences.zh: 但我们也不想要来自工业界的框架和言辞；我们拒绝恶意设计的概念、可悲的销售宣传、无知的争论。

sentences.en: No, if AI is a vague term, one cannot conclude some AI may be useful.
sentences.zh: 不，如果人工智能是一个模糊的术语，我们就不能断定某些人工智能可能有用。

sentences.en: No, Google's Alphafold is not scientific and not a different kind of technology.
sentences.zh: 不，谷歌的 Alphafold 不是科学的，也不是一种不同的技术。

sentences.en: It's built on very similar formalisms — and perhaps even more importantly, constitutes the corporate capture of biology.
sentences.zh: 它建立在非常相似的形式主义之上——也许更重要的是，构成了对生物学的企业捕获。

sentences.en: Yes, such models are barely scientific.
sentences.zh: 是的，这样的模型几乎不科学。

sentences.en: Thank goodness Google has killed it both as a product and as an excuse for these kinds of anti-scientific claims.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，谷歌已经将其作为一种产品和此类反科学主张的借口而消灭了。

blocks.html_en: AI's way of thinking is not just anti-science, but spills into pseudoscience and other forms of complete detachment from reality. Core to the anxiety I am experiencing is that I feel so many around me have become unmoored from ethical and practical concerns, like keeping universities going, and attached instead to nonsense, to put it mildly. Nikhil Suresh explains this:

sentences.en: AI's way of thinking is not just anti-science, but spills into pseudoscience and other forms of complete detachment from reality.
sentences.zh: 人工智能的思维方式不仅是反科学的，而且还渗透到伪科学和其他完全脱离现实的形式。

sentences.en: Core to the anxiety I am experiencing is that I feel so many around me have become unmoored from ethical and practical concerns, like keeping universities going, and attached instead to nonsense, to put it mildly.
sentences.zh: 我所经历的焦虑的核心是，我觉得我周围的许多人已经脱离了道德和实际问题，比如让大学继续运转，而委婉地说，他们执着于胡言乱语。

sentences.en: Nikhil Suresh explains this:
sentences.zh: 尼基尔·苏雷什解释道：

blocks.html_en: "Executives that tell the press that their company has gone insane will quickly find themselves removed from their positions. Employees who are honest will find themselves fired in short-order, or 'randomly' selected for a round of layoffs. In fact, it is in the interests of almost every actor in the space — boards, executives, employees, vendors, consultants — to obfuscate and misrepresent the success rate of AI projects. Many publicly traded companies are putting out announcements about their AI productivity gains when I know for a fact that the businesses have done nothing other than purchase Copilot licenses and declare victory."

sentences.en: "Executives that tell the press that their company has gone insane will quickly find themselves removed from their positions.
sentences.zh: “那些告诉媒体他们的公司已经疯了的高管很快就会发现自己被撤职了。

sentences.en: Employees who are honest will find themselves fired in short-order, or 'randomly' selected for a round of layoffs.
sentences.zh: 诚实的员工会发现自己很快被解雇，或者“随机”被选中进行一轮裁员。

sentences.en: In fact, it is in the interests of almost every actor in the space — boards, executives, employees, vendors, consultants — to obfuscate and misrepresent the success rate of AI projects.
sentences.zh: 事实上，混淆和歪曲人工智能项目的成功率符合该领域几乎所有参与者（董事会、高管、员工、供应商、顾问）的利益。

sentences.en: Many publicly traded companies are putting out announcements about their AI productivity gains when I know for a fact that the businesses have done nothing other than purchase Copilot licenses and declare victory."
sentences.zh: 许多上市公司都在发布有关人工智能生产力提升的公告，而我知道这些企业除了购买 Copilot 许可证并宣布胜利之外什么也没做。”

blocks.html_en: Universities have done this too. And we best listen to those who blow these whistles before it's too late.

sentences.en: Universities have done this too.
sentences.zh: 大学也这样做了。

sentences.en: And we best listen to those who blow these whistles before it's too late.
sentences.zh: 我们最好倾听那些吹哨人的声音，以免为时已晚。

blocks.html_en: OK, so I had a few panic attacks because I realised the fabric of trust between me and my students, especially my closer mentees, was pretty thin. And also damaged is the belief that my colleagues, and even the university in general, have similar goals, like a love of learning and of teaching, a respect and appreciation for our jobs, a deep care for the psychological landscapes we all inhabit, and a need to cultivate our social relationships. Recall how like AI extracts labour, I witness senior colleagues extract from juniors their mental, and especially emotional, labour, offloading stress and cognitive processing onto others. And most disturbingly, pushing onto them this labour in their time of need. AI's logics do this to us too. Attacking educators and researchers is not a coincidence, but a group of people vulnerable after many rounds of funding cuts and anti-scientific and anti-humanistic thinking.

sentences.en: OK, so I had a few panic attacks because I realised the fabric of trust between me and my students, especially my closer mentees, was pretty thin.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我有过几次惊恐发作，因为我意识到我和我的学生，尤其是我的亲密学员之间的信任结构非常薄弱。

sentences.en: And also damaged is the belief that my colleagues, and even the university in general, have similar goals, like a love of learning and of teaching, a respect and appreciation for our jobs, a deep care for the psychological landscapes we all inhabit, and a need to cultivate our social relationships.
sentences.zh: 同样受到损害的是我的同事们，甚至整个大学，都有相似的目标的信念，比如热爱学习和教学，尊重和欣赏我们的工作，深切关注我们所有人所居住的心理景观，以及培养我们的社会关系的需要。

sentences.en: Recall how like AI extracts labour, I witness senior colleagues extract from juniors their mental, and especially emotional, labour, offloading stress and cognitive processing onto others.
sentences.zh: 回想一下人工智能如何榨取劳动力，我亲眼目睹高级同事从初级同事那里榨取他们的精神劳动，尤其是情感劳动，将压力和认知处理转移给他人。

sentences.en: And most disturbingly, pushing onto them this labour in their time of need.
sentences.zh: 最令人不安的是，在他们需要的时候把这项工作强加给他们。

sentences.en: AI's logics do this to us too.
sentences.zh: 人工智能的逻辑对我们也有同样的作用。

sentences.en: Attacking educators and researchers is not a coincidence, but a group of people vulnerable after many rounds of funding cuts and anti-scientific and anti-humanistic thinking.
sentences.zh: 攻击教育工作者和研究人员并不是巧合，而是经过多轮资金削减和反科学、反人文思潮后的弱势群体。

blocks.html_en: So what can we learn from this? Well, firstly, the obvious: be kind to ourselves if we feel the walls closing in because... well, yes, they are, so we need all the mental and physical fortitude we can muster. But, and perhaps more importantly than the well-known "take care of ourselves and others", we must keep at the forefront: this is what AI companies want. They want us to falter and get sick. They want us to have panic attacks, which sure, we will have, but — and this is the really vital bit — we will strive not to resolve the panic by allowing AI logics in.

sentences.en: So what can we learn from this?
sentences.zh: 那么我们可以从中学到什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, firstly, the obvious: be kind to ourselves if we feel the walls closing in because...
sentences.zh: 好吧，首先，显而易见的是：如果我们感到墙壁正在关闭，请善待自己，因为……

sentences.en: well, yes, they are, so we need all the mental and physical fortitude we can muster.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，他们是，所以我们需要我们能聚集的所有精神和身体上的毅力。

sentences.en: But, and perhaps more importantly than the well-known "take care of ourselves and others", we must keep at the forefront: this is what AI companies want.
sentences.zh: 但是，也许比众所周知的“照顾自己和他人”更重要的是，我们必须走在最前沿：这就是人工智能公司想要的。

sentences.en: They want us to falter and get sick.
sentences.zh: 他们希望我们步履蹒跚并生病。

sentences.en: They want us to have panic attacks, which sure, we will have, but — and this is the really vital bit — we will strive not to resolve the panic by allowing AI logics in.
sentences.zh: 他们希望我们发生恐慌，当然，我们会发生这种情况，但是——这是真正重要的一点——我们将努力不通过允许人工智能逻辑进入来解决恐慌。

blocks.html_en: Argument from ignorance, which a panic attack might trigger, is not valid: there is no good AI, just because it's a confusing terminological mess. The same goes for descent into using AI-detection tools. Just because some prose may look like it's written using an AI tool, in fact there is no such thing as automated plagiarism detection software. They are a scam sold by the very same companies that create the AI systems used for plagiarism in the first place. And companies through such so-called tools want to further erode our trust in each other.

sentences.en: Argument from ignorance, which a panic attack might trigger, is not valid: there is no good AI, just because it's a confusing terminological mess.
sentences.zh: 恐慌发作可能引发的无知论据是无效的：没有好的人工智能，只是因为它是一个令人困惑的术语混乱。

sentences.en: The same goes for descent into using AI-detection tools.
sentences.zh: 使用人工智能检测工具也是如此。

sentences.en: Just because some prose may look like it's written using an AI tool, in fact there is no such thing as automated plagiarism detection software.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为有些散文看起来像是用人工智能工具写的，事实上并不存在自动抄袭检测软件之类的东西。

sentences.en: They are a scam sold by the very same companies that create the AI systems used for plagiarism in the first place.
sentences.zh: 它们是由最初创建用于抄袭的人工智能系统的同一家公司出售的骗局。

sentences.en: And companies through such so-called tools want to further erode our trust in each other.
sentences.zh: 公司希望通过此类所谓的工具进一步削弱我们对彼此的信任。

blocks.html_en: Nor is it OK to allow AI to rule us by guiding our teaching — in fact I and my coauthors implore us not to

sentences.en: Nor is it OK to allow AI to rule us by guiding our teaching — in fact I and my coauthors implore us not to
sentences.zh: 让人工智能通过指导我们的教学来统治我们也是不对的——事实上，我和我的合著者恳求我们不要这样做

blocks.html_en: "allow AI, neither as bully nor so-called tool, to redefine our roles as educators or researchers. It is not our job to chase hype. What this means is by all means educators should feel empowered and inspired by the urgency to uplift students, but not to use AI to do so."

sentences.en: "allow AI, neither as bully nor so-called tool, to redefine our roles as educators or researchers.
sentences.zh: “让人工智能，无论是作为恶霸还是所谓的工具，重新定义我们作为教育者或研究人员的角色。

sentences.en: It is not our job to chase hype.
sentences.zh: 追逐炒作不是我们的工作。

sentences.en: What this means is by all means educators should feel empowered and inspired by the urgency to uplift students, but not to use AI to do so."
sentences.zh: 这意味着教育工作者应该因提升学生的紧迫性而感到被赋予权力和受到启发，但不要使用人工智能来做到这一点。”

blocks.html_en: We also do not need to obey in advance as some love to do under increasing fascism. As Timothy Snyder explains:

sentences.en: We also do not need to obey in advance as some love to do under increasing fascism.
sentences.zh: 我们也不需要像法西斯主义日益猖獗的情况下某些人喜欢做的那样提前服从。

sentences.en: As Timothy Snyder explains:
sentences.zh: 正如蒂莫西·斯奈德所解释的：

blocks.html_en: "Most of the power of authoritarianism is freely given. In times like these, individuals think ahead about what a more repressive government will want, and then offer themselves without being asked. A citizen who adapts in this way is teaching power what it can do."

sentences.en: "Most of the power of authoritarianism is freely given.
sentences.zh: “威权主义的大部分权力都是自由赋予的。

sentences.en: In times like these, individuals think ahead about what a more repressive government will want, and then offer themselves without being asked.
sentences.zh: 在这样的时代，个人会提前思考一个更具压制性的政府会想要什么，然后在没有被询问的情况下提出自己的要求。

sentences.en: A citizen who adapts in this way is teaching power what it can do."
sentences.zh: 以这种方式适应的公民正在教导权力它能做什么。”

blocks.html_en: In our capacity as academics, perhaps the most radical thing we can do is our job itself. How can anybody in their right mind notice the growing damage to universities and instead of stand against this, facilitate the destruction of expertise, of learning skills, and of academic integrity? And the simplest stand is to refuse all the frames that want us scared and distrustful and instead embrace just doing our jobs and supporting each other.

sentences.en: In our capacity as academics, perhaps the most radical thing we can do is our job itself.
sentences.zh: 作为学者，我们能做的最激进的事情也许就是我们的工作本身。

sentences.en: How can anybody in their right mind notice the growing damage to universities and instead of stand against this, facilitate the destruction of expertise, of learning skills, and of academic integrity?
sentences.zh: 任何心智正常的人怎么可能注意到大学受到的损害日益严重，而不是反对这一点，反而助长了专业知识、学习技能和学术诚信的破坏？

sentences.en: And the simplest stand is to refuse all the frames that want us scared and distrustful and instead embrace just doing our jobs and supporting each other.
sentences.zh: 最简单的立场就是拒绝所有让我们感到害怕和不信任的框架，而是拥抱只做好我们的工作并互相支持。

blocks.html_en: can an individual make a difference?

sentences.en: can an individual make a difference?
sentences.zh: 一个人能有所作为吗？

content_html_zh:
焦虑通常与压力不同，只是焦虑持续存在，甚至在压力源消失后仍然存在。 但人工智能显然一直存在，总是与一切交织在一起…… 所以谁知道我的感受。 我很难真正理解自己有时有多不舒服，因为在人工智能的推动下，一切感觉都被侵蚀了。 自从5年前加入AI相关部门以来，至少对我来说，一切都被彻底感染了。

我将提出一些想法，希望这个练习可以为他人提供一些帮助，为我自己带来治愈，并可能最终在让我们所有人摆脱困境的道路上放上一块小石子——就像尼基尔·苏雷什（Nikhil Suresh）所说的“让那些试图在这一切中生存的人们放心，他们没有疯。” 还要感谢劳伦·弗雷泽（Lauren Fraser）这样的人，他们说他们可能有兴趣听听我将在下面重复的内容。

你可能想知道这种情感提取和混乱与人工智能有什么关系。 它与人工智能息息相关。 或者更确切地说，人工智能与它息息相关。 情感抽取和压迫是由人工智能制定的——这些力量的运行方式相似，即弱势群体的心理疲惫在让我们保持原状方面发挥着积极作用。

从另一个角度来看：简单地说，法西斯人工智能及其所有症状迫使我们中的一些学者面对我们的同谋、我们的相互交织以及采取立场的道德义务。 我不会默默地参与从受训者和学生那里获取信息，无论是他们的数据、他们的情感和认知劳动，还是其他任何东西。 我不会袖手旁观，让大学被掏空和摧毁。 一个不完美的机构需要改进，而不是卖给出价最低的人——或者可悲的是，更准确地说，不应该向最邪恶的公司支付认购费。

阿卜杜勒贾瓦德·奥马尔 (Abdaljawad Omar) 将西方学术界和社会概括为

“一个倾听主体已经加强了对所听到内容的影响的抵抗，一种将真理变成噪音的政治话语，将甚至最详尽的文件转化为另一轮受管理的不确定性的机会，并且已经学会将情报语法作为其取消赎回权的工具。 [...] 西方知识分子的怯懦是真实存在的：岔路口已经存在，选择已经做出，责任并没有通过称之为结构性而得到消除。”

在人工智能在巴勒斯坦引发种族灭绝的时代，我们看到人工智能公司大声疾呼为美国攻击伊朗提供便利，并公开炫耀他们对地球毁灭的贡献，我们也目睹了大学的损失。 我们向公司出售的产品如此之多，甚至没有被所有人视为利益冲突。 我们只有一份工作。 作为学者，我们的职责是保护这一机构。 这就是我们收到税款的原因；为什么我们基本上是公务员。 许多人甚至忽视了大学的作用，因此需要重复一遍：提供最高水平的知识和教育。 人工智能从根本上摧毁了两者。 它暴露了我们中的一些人是困惑的，我们中的一些人是机会主义者，而这两个群体都是懦夫，他们宁愿提取而不是反思，宁愿快速行动并打破常规，也不愿学会遵循缓慢而有条理的学术实践实践。

人工智能加入战局

这种情感的抽离和骚动也是非常个人化的。 作为一名心智正常的学者，当我们发现我们的同事、上级以及大学各个层面的管理人员都对这一切感到满意时，谁不会感到被背叛、愤怒、精神错乱——这是我们世界观的粉碎？ 他们对共谋种族灭绝、国内外的校园屠杀、破坏自己的大学本身并不介意。

我无数次哭泣、失眠…… 新的一天是失去信心的新机会，是从焦虑到恐惧到抑郁再到上述所有情况的新水平。 为什么我的很多同事，尤其是那些有权力采取行动的同事却看不到这一点？ 他们为什么不关心？ 我们所有带着痛苦而不是真正提问的人都知道为什么。 人工智能是一个法西斯项目，它促成了所有这些环环相扣的事件。 我们以前来过这里。

这种情感的抽离和骚动也延伸到了一切事物上。 意识到学生们也被推入这个泥潭：我可以相信我自己的学员吗？ 我发现自己在没有充分理由的情况下认为学生的作业是人工智能生成的。 仅仅因为这项工作非常好，我们一起工作了几个月，我就焦虑不安，而且我对每个人的信任都很脆弱，我认为它可能会被人工智能感染。 我查看了文件并查看了历史编辑。 没有人工智能的证据，但只是逐渐意识到我和其他像我一样的人可能会失去我们的控制，已经失去了对信任同事或受训者意味着什么的控制。 我应该有信心相信我的初级合作者，而无需查看编辑历史记录。

那一刻我深深地恨自己。 我记得哭得很厉害。 我还闪回了许多其他不愉快的感觉，因为同事们拒绝了我的原则、研究领域，以及某些人实际上确实值得听到他们的声音的想法。 在这样的时刻，一切都混合在一起。 我真的让这一切都发生在我身上。

第二次这些想法出现在我脑海中时，我感到很熟悉，但记忆无助于阻止焦虑重新滋长、溃烂。 我感到非常不舒服，非常讨厌自己有这些想法，指责别人，即使只是在我的脑海里。 我睡了大约两天。 当我希望世界消失时，为什么我应该垂直于世界？

作为学者，我们不断要求雇主倾听我们的意见，了解我们的要求是关于大学作为一个机构的未来，关于推翻我们所知道的专业知识和技能学习。 我们不想要微软的无意义产品。 但我们也不想要来自工业界的框架和言辞；我们拒绝恶意设计的概念、可悲的销售宣传、无知的争论。 不，如果人工智能是一个模糊的术语，我们就不能断定某些人工智能可能有用。 不，谷歌的 Alphafold 不是科学的，也不是一种不同的技术。 它建立在非常相似的形式主义之上——也许更重要的是，构成了对生物学的企业捕获。 是的，这样的模型几乎不科学。 谢天谢地，谷歌已经将其作为一种产品和此类反科学主张的借口而消灭了。

人工智能的思维方式不仅是反科学的，而且还渗透到伪科学和其他完全脱离现实的形式。 我所经历的焦虑的核心是，我觉得我周围的许多人已经脱离了道德和实际问题，比如让大学继续运转，而委婉地说，他们执着于胡言乱语。 尼基尔·苏雷什解释道：

“那些告诉媒体他们的公司已经疯了的高管很快就会发现自己被撤职了。 诚实的员工会发现自己很快被解雇，或者“随机”被选中进行一轮裁员。 事实上，混淆和歪曲人工智能项目的成功率符合该领域几乎所有参与者（董事会、高管、员工、供应商、顾问）的利益。 许多上市公司都在发布有关人工智能生产力提升的公告，而我知道这些企业除了购买 Copilot 许可证并宣布胜利之外什么也没做。”

大学也这样做了。 我们最好倾听那些吹哨人的声音，以免为时已晚。

好吧，我有过几次惊恐发作，因为我意识到我和我的学生，尤其是我的亲密学员之间的信任结构非常薄弱。 同样受到损害的是我的同事们，甚至整个大学，都有相似的目标的信念，比如热爱学习和教学，尊重和欣赏我们的工作，深切关注我们所有人所居住的心理景观，以及培养我们的社会关系的需要。 回想一下人工智能如何榨取劳动力，我亲眼目睹高级同事从初级同事那里榨取他们的精神劳动，尤其是情感劳动，将压力和认知处理转移给他人。 最令人不安的是，在他们需要的时候把这项工作强加给他们。 人工智能的逻辑对我们也有同样的作用。 攻击教育工作者和研究人员并不是巧合，而是经过多轮资金削减和反科学、反人文思潮后的弱势群体。

那么我们可以从中学到什么呢？ 好吧，首先，显而易见的是：如果我们感到墙壁正在关闭，请善待自己，因为…… 嗯，是的，他们是，所以我们需要我们能聚集的所有精神和身体上的毅力。 但是，也许比众所周知的“照顾自己和他人”更重要的是，我们必须走在最前沿：这就是人工智能公司想要的。 他们希望我们步履蹒跚并生病。 他们希望我们发生恐慌，当然，我们会发生这种情况，但是——这是真正重要的一点——我们将努力不通过允许人工智能逻辑进入来解决恐慌。

恐慌发作可能引发的无知论据是无效的：没有好的人工智能，只是因为它是一个令人困惑的术语混乱。 使用人工智能检测工具也是如此。 仅仅因为有些散文看起来像是用人工智能工具写的，事实上并不存在自动抄袭检测软件之类的东西。 它们是由最初创建用于抄袭的人工智能系统的同一家公司出售的骗局。 公司希望通过此类所谓的工具进一步削弱我们对彼此的信任。

让人工智能通过指导我们的教学来统治我们也是不对的——事实上，我和我的合著者恳求我们不要这样做

“让人工智能，无论是作为恶霸还是所谓的工具，重新定义我们作为教育者或研究人员的角色。 追逐炒作不是我们的工作。 这意味着教育工作者应该因提升学生的紧迫性而感到被赋予权力和受到启发，但不要使用人工智能来做到这一点。”

我们也不需要像法西斯主义日益猖獗的情况下某些人喜欢做的那样提前服从。 正如蒂莫西·斯奈德所解释的：

“威权主义的大部分权力都是自由赋予的。 在这样的时代，个人会提前思考一个更具压制性的政府会想要什么，然后在没有被询问的情况下提出自己的要求。 以这种方式适应的公民正在教导权力它能做什么。”

作为学者，我们能做的最激进的事情也许就是我们的工作本身。 任何心智正常的人怎么可能注意到大学受到的损害日益严重，而不是反对这一点，反而助长了专业知识、学习技能和学术诚信的破坏？ 最简单的立场就是拒绝所有让我们感到害怕和不信任的框架，而是拥抱只做好我们的工作并互相支持。

一个人能有所作为吗？
